Let \(y_i=\cos x_i\). Then \(y_i\in[-1,1]\), \(\sum_{i=1}^{10}y_i=0\), and
\[
\cos(3x_i)=4\cos^3x_i-3\cos x_i=4y_i^3-3y_i.
\]
Thus
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{10}\cos(3x_i)
=4\sum_{i=1}^{10}y_i^3-3\sum_{i=1}^{10}y_i
=4\sum_{i=1}^{10}y_i^3.
\]
So we maximize \(\sum y_i^3\) subject to \(y_i\in[-1,1]\) and \(\sum y_i=0\).

At the maximum, positive \(y_i\)'s are concentrated as \(1,1,\dots,r\), while the remaining negative values are equal. If there are \(p\) positive values, write the positive total as
\[
S=p-1+r,\qquad 0\le r\le 1.
\]
Then the negative values are all \(-\frac{S}{10-p}\), so
\[
\sum y_i^3=(p-1)+r^3-\frac{(p-1+r)^3}{(10-p)^2}.
\]
Checking \(p=1,2,3,4,5\), the maximum occurs at \(p=3,\ r=1\):
\[
\sum y_i^3=3-\frac{3^3}{7^2}
=3-\frac{27}{49}
=\frac{120}{49}.
\]
This is attained by \(y_1=y_2=y_3=1\) and \(y_4=\cdots=y_{10}=-\frac37\), which satisfy \(\sum y_i=0\). Therefore
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{10}\cos(3x_i)
=4\cdot \frac{120}{49}
=\boxed{\frac{480}{49}}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{480}{49}}
\]
